firmographics_and_context: EU Telco innovation lab attached to a large telecom group. They run pilots for internal customer support + NOC automation, then hand off to central platform team for production. Strong preference for EU vendors/hosting and strict governance on where data and logs live. Partner involved (regional SI / cloud marketplace co-sell) and wants a reusable “EU-only demo + eval” motion.
key_requirements_summary: Must-have: EU data residency (prompts/outputs + derived telemetry), ability to constrain routing/fallback to EU regions only, private networking (VPC/VNet peering), SSO/SAML with RBAC, audit logs exportable to their SIEM, configurable retention (including shorter retention) and KMS-backed encryption. Nice-to-have: on-prem option for later phases (some sites have restricted connectivity).
workload_notes: Initial pilot workloads are mostly chat + summarization (customer care transcripts, KB articles, incident summaries) and doc-search/RAG (internal ops docs). They care about predictable latency for agent assist; less sensitive on absolute model choice as long as performance and governance are solid. Interested in running evals with their own prompt sets but want guidance so the pilot doesn’t become a full bespoke POC.
demo_notes: Ran standard demo but emphasized: (1) deployment flexibility (Hosted → Dedicated → Private), (2) routing/fallback policies (and what constraints are supported), (3) Console observability (token cost/latency) + error analysis. They asked: “If Frankfurt is degraded, do you ever route to US by default?” and “Where do logs live, and can we keep them EU-only?” We were careful to separate: what we can show live in the demo tenant vs what is configurable in Dedicated/Private. They reacted well to the notion of pinned model versions + controlled rollouts, but want written commitments for residency + operational controls.
partner_involvement: Partner (regional SI) is pushing a joint plan: Redwood provides Dedicated (EU) or Private (VPC) + partner handles network connectivity, identity integration, and initial app wiring. They requested a partner-friendly slide: ‘EU-only routing + logging posture’ and a lightweight evaluation checklist to avoid reinventing each pilot.
internal_notes: Avoid quoting specific latency numbers; they asked for benchmarks but we should stick to approved ranges and propose running a controlled benchmark during eval. Also: watch for quota/throttle confusion if we do a shared demo tenant run again—keep defaults demo-safe and have plan B canned outputs if variability comes up.
